papers.title: Developing New Methods for Comparing Treatments in Case-Control Studies
papers.one_line: A PCORI research summary reports new methods and a guide for analyzing case-control data so that results resemble a randomized trial, validated on a single exposure and outcome pair, statins and heart attack, in Washington State health records.
papers.what_was_done: The project developed analytic methods and a written guide for applying trial-emulation logic to case-control data, on the stated premise that existing methods work for cohort designs but not for case-control designs. Researchers who conduct case-control studies were interviewed, the guide was drafted from what they reported, and it was revised after a second round of feedback. A computer program was written to implement the analysis. The methods were tested on health records from Washington State health systems by running both a case-control and a cohort study of statins for the prevention of heart attack, and comparing the results with previously published randomized trials of statins. The reported outcome of that comparison is that the new case-control methods were more accurate than existing case-control methods and than existing cohort methods. No effect estimates, sample sizes, intervals or replication metrics appear in the public summary. Two limits are stated: the methods require data collected at multiple time points, and the validation covers one treatment and one outcome.

future_research.gap: Whether the method transfers beyond the single validated exposure and outcome is untested
future_research.quote: Future research could test if the new methods work for other health problems or treatments.
future_research.locator: What were the limits of the project?

problems.evidence: The whole evidentiary basis for the new case-control methods is one exposure and one outcome, statins and heart attack, benchmarked against statin trials, and the project itself flags that as a limit. Nothing in the design licenses carrying that success to a different drug class, a different outcome or a different data source, and no argument is offered for why agreement on a well-studied cardiovascular question predicts agreement anywhere else.
problems.quote: The research team tested the new methods using data for one treatment for heart attacks.
problems.locator: What were the limits of the project?

problems.evidence: The result of the trial comparison is reported as an ordinal claim, that the new methods were more accurate than two comparators, with no estimate, no interval and no statement of what quantity the case-control analysis and the trial each targeted. A reader cannot tell whether the improvement was a shift of a few percent in a hazard ratio or a sign change, nor whether the case-control estimand matched the trial estimand at all.
problems.quote: Compared with current methods for case-control and cohort studies, the new methods for case-control studies got more accurate results.

problems.evidence: The two deliverables named are a guide and a computer program, and the public record of the project describes their existence and points readers to a project page rather than to a versioned repository. The phenotype logic used to build the Washington State cohorts, the code that produced the comparison against the statin trials, and the intermediate case-control specifications that were rejected are all absent from the record, so the reported accuracy improvement cannot be reproduced or audited from what is published.
problems.quote: The research team also created a computer program to analyze case-control data.

papers.title: Emulating a Randomised Controlled Trial With Observational Data: An Introduction to the Target Trial Framework.
papers.one_line: A cardiology tutorial on the target trial framework works through the RCT DUPLICATE emulation of TRITON-TIMI-38, which reproduced the trial MACE hazard ratio of 0.81 with 0.83 under both on-treatment and as-started analyses while recovering only 13,670 of 305,112 Optum patients who underwent PCI.
papers.what_was_done: Seven design elements, eligibility, treatment assignment, time zero, outcomes, follow-up, causal contrasts and analysis, are set out and then applied to the RCT DUPLICATE emulation of prasugrel versus clopidogrel dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention. Time zero was the day after outpatient therapy began, which had to occur within 14 days of hospital discharge; exposure persisted for the length of a prescription plus a 30-day grace period. Over 120 covariates were assembled from ICD codes and 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity matching with a 0.01 caliper was applied. Of 305,112 Optum and 433,641 MarketScan patients who underwent PCI, 39,448 and 66,003 met criteria and 13,670 and 30,194 remained after matching. MACE incidence in the emulation was 4.4 percent versus 3.3 percent, against 11.5 percent versus 9.4 percent in TRITON; history of myocardial infarction was 7.8 to 8 percent against 18 percent in the trial. The on-treatment analysis gave a hazard ratio of 0.83 (0.74 to 0.95) and the as-started analysis 0.83 (0.73 to 0.95), against the trial's 0.81 (0.73 to 0.90); bleeding was 1.17 (1.01 to 1.34) against 1.32 (1.03 to 1.68). Outcome codes carried reported positive predictive values of 88.4 to 94 percent for myocardial infarction, 85 percent for ischemic stroke and 80 to 90 percent for hemorrhagic stroke. Across the ten RCT DUPLICATE emulations, seven target trials had to substitute an active drug for a placebo arm.

future_research.gap: No procedure exists for constructing a comparator that stands in for a placebo arm in claims data
future_research.quote: reported “moderate” to “poor” placebo emulation in the health claims datasets, which highlights the difficulties of identifying a proper comparison group to represent the “placebo arm” when using real-world data.

problems.evidence: Seven of the ten trials selected for emulation were placebo-controlled, and the placebo arm was replaced by an antidiabetic drug chosen for having similar indications. The resulting emulation quality is graded as moderate to poor, which records that the substitution failed without supplying any rule for when one active drug is a defensible stand-in for no drug. The equivalence class here is defined by shared indication alone, and shared indication is exactly the property that makes the substitute pharmacologically active on the outcome.
problems.quote: The “standard-of-care” was emulated through selecting an antidiabetic medication with similar treatment indications as the drug under investigation.

problems.evidence: Three timing parameters carry the design: time zero is the day after outpatient therapy starts, the therapy must start within 14 days of discharge or the patient is dropped, and exposure persists for a prescription plus 30 days. Each of these is a free choice that redefines both the eligible set and the exposure, and none is fixed by a stated outcome-blind procedure. Widening the 14-day window changes who enters; lengthening the 30-day grace changes when the on-treatment analysis censors and therefore changes the reported 0.83.
problems.quote: Target trial participants were considered exposed for the full length of a prescription plus a grace period of 30 days if no new prescription was initiated.
problems.locator: Target trial case study, Treatment status

problems.evidence: Three trial exclusions have no counterpart in claims: over-the-counter NSAID use, intolerance to dual antiplatelet therapy, and fibrinolytic therapy. Patients with any of these are retained because the data cannot show them, so the emulated eligible set of 39,448 and 66,003 patients is one in which absence of record and absence of the condition are the same thing, and the resulting comparison is reported against a trial whose population excluded them.
problems.quote: the health claims did not capture all exclusion criteria applied in the original RCT (e.g. Over the counter NSAID use, intolerance to a DAPT, and fibrinolytic therapy).

problems.evidence: Positive predictive values are reported for every outcome code, 88.4 to 94 percent for myocardial infarction, 85 percent for ischemic stroke and 80 to 90 percent for hemorrhagic stroke, and are then not used. The outcomes enter the Cox model as binary events, MACE incidence comes out at 4.4 percent against 11.5 percent in the trial, and the hazard ratio of 0.83 with its interval of 0.74 to 0.95 carries no contribution from the known imperfect ascertainment. Reporting a validation statistic and reporting an error-free variable are done in the same paragraph.
problems.quote: used validated ICD-9/10 codes to define MI (PPV ranged from 88.4% to 94%), ischemic strokes (PPV 85%), hemorrhagic strokes (PPV 80% to 90%)

problems.evidence: The databases hold 305,112 and 433,641 patients who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. Eligibility restriction removes 87 and 85 percent of them, and 1:1 propensity matching removes most of what remains, leaving 13,670 and 30,194, that is 4.5 and 7.0 percent of the starting counts. The size advantage over a randomized trial that motivates using these databases has largely been spent before the first estimate is computed, and neither the effective sample nor the loss at each step is treated as a quantity the design must report.
problems.quote: After 1:1 PS matching 13,670 and 30,194 were included in the analyses, from their respective datasets

problems.evidence: Success is adjudicated by regulatory agreement, defined as reproducing the direction and the statistical significance of the trial result. Under that rule the ticagrelor emulation at 0.92 (0.83 to 1.02) is a failure against PLATO at 0.84 (0.77 to 0.92) even though the intervals overlap, while an emulation whose point estimate sat far from the trial's would pass provided both cleared significance. A binary that keys on a p-value boundary is not a calibrated comparison of estimands, and the tutorial's own defense of the ticagrelor case is that other trials also failed to replicate PLATO.
problems.quote: In terms of regulatory agreement, defined as “the ability of the [target trial] study to replicate the direction and statistical significance of the RCT finding”

papers.title: Computational drug repositioning of atorvastatin for ulcerative colitis.
papers.one_line: A transcriptomic repurposing signal for atorvastatin in ulcerative colitis was tested in two claims and EHR cohorts structured as a target trial emulation, giving colectomy hazard ratios of 0.47 in STARR (n = 827) and 0.66 in Optum (n = 7821).
papers.what_was_done: A 2306-gene ulcerative colitis signature built from 272 colon biopsy samples across 11 GEO datasets was correlated against LINCS L1000 profiles for 781 FDA-approved drugs, and atorvastatin was carried forward to an active-comparator emulation in two databases. The Stanford STARR EHR contributed 827 patients (231 atorvastatin, 596 comparator) and Optum Clinformatics contributed 7821 (2881 atorvastatin, 4940 comparator); the comparator arm pooled benazepril, furosemide, losartan, propranolol, hydralazine, niacin, ezetimibe, cholestyramine, omega 3 fatty acids and metformin into a single treatment strategy. Time zero was the first recorded prescription after the first recorded UC diagnosis, with no minimum treatment duration required. Adjusted Cox models gave colectomy hazard ratios of 0.43 (0.21 to 0.88) in STARR and 0.67 (0.46 to 0.97) in Optum, and propensity-score matching gave 0.46 (0.22 to 0.98) and 0.64 (0.41 to 0.88). Colectomy incidence differed fourfold across the two sources, 9.4 percent in STARR versus 2.3 percent in Optum, from the same ICD-coded outcome definition. A negative control outcome, pneumonia, showed no association in either source. A secondary contrast restricted atorvastatin users to those followed at least 720 days and split them at six months of prescribed therapy, giving a hazard ratio of 0.32 (0.11 to 0.95). Smoking, disease phenotype and nonprescription drug use were not available in either source.

future_research.gap: Whether the observational colectomy signal reflects a treatment effect is left to a trial
future_research.quote: Prospective controlled clinical trials are needed to confirm whether atorvastatin treatment would benefit patients with UC.

problems.evidence: The comparator strategy pools ten drugs from two pharmacologic classes into one arm: an ACE inhibitor, a loop diuretic, an angiotensin receptor blocker, a beta blocker, a vasodilator, niacin, ezetimibe, a bile acid sequestrant, fish oil and metformin. The stated criterion for membership is that a drug is prescription-only and intended for long-term use, which is an administrative property rather than a pharmacologic or clinical one. No procedure is given that would decide whether metformin and cholestyramine belong in the same equivalence class for a colectomy outcome, and the hazard ratios of 0.43 and 0.67 are reported against that pooled arm as if it named one treatment.
problems.quote: The comparator drugs were prescription-only first or second line therapies intended for long-term treatment for cardiovascular conditions
problems.locator: Materials and Methods, Cohort identification and assessment of exposures

problems.evidence: The same colectomy phenotype yields 9.4 percent incidence in the EHR source and 2.3 percent in the claims source, a fourfold gap attributed to differential procedure reporting. That is a direct measurement of outcome ascertainment error across the two databases, yet the outcome enters both Cox models as an error-free binary and the two hazard ratios, 0.47 and 0.66, are reported side by side with no propagation of the known misclassification into either interval.
problems.quote: The apparent discrepancy in colectomy rate can be explained by previously noted lower procedure reporting in claims data compared to EHRs.
problems.locator: Results, Atorvastatin use in patients with UC is associated with decreased risk of colectomy

problems.evidence: The primary analysis deliberately imposes no minimum treatment duration to avoid immortal time, but the secondary long-term versus short-term contrast then restricts to patients followed at least 720 days and splits them at six months of prescribed therapy, producing a hazard ratio of 0.32 (0.11 to 0.95). Both the 720-day restriction and the six-month cut point are post-baseline classifications with no outcome-blind rule that fixed them; a different threshold defines a different exposure and a different eligible set.
problems.quote: We subset atorvastatin-treated patients to those that were followed for at least 720 days from the initiation of the drug
problems.locator: Results, Sensitivity analysis of dose and duration of treatment

problems.evidence: A negative control outcome is deployed and reported: pneumonia risk is unaffected by atorvastatin in both sources, chosen because statin use appears protective for pneumonia when healthy-user bias is uncontrolled. That is one negative control embedded in the emulation rather than left to a separate literature. It does not close the entry: the control returns a qualitative pass or fail, no negative control exposure or proxy is used, no validation sample calibrates the residual bias, and the pneumonia null is not converted into a bound on the 0.47 and 0.66 colectomy estimates.
problems.quote: the lack of pneumonia protection due to statin use in our cohorts supports that the structure of this study minimizes the healthy user bias
problems.locator: Results, Atorvastatin use in patients with UC is associated with decreased risk of colectomy

problems.evidence: Disease phenotype, smoking history and nonprescription drug use are all absent from both sources, and colectomy is conceded to be an imperfect marker of the construct of interest. These deficiencies are recorded in prose after the fact, and the analysis proceeds to publish two hazard ratios; no threshold on covariate availability or outcome validity was set in advance that would have stopped the emulation at either source.
problems.quote: given the limitations of administrative data, we were unable to examine the potentially important effects of disease phenotype, smoking history, or use of nonprescription drugs in our cohort studies

papers.title: Exploring the feasibility of using real-world data from a large clinical data research network to simulate clinical trials of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.one_line: A phase III donepezil trial was resimulated from the OneFlorida network, where only 25 of 36 eligibility criteria were computable and the incomputable ones were resolved by declaring every candidate eligible, leaving 38 patients in the 23 mg arm.
papers.what_was_done: Trial NCT00478205, comparing 23 mg sustained-release donepezil with 10 mg immediate-release donepezil in moderate to severe Alzheimer disease, was reconstructed from the OneFlorida clinical data research network, which covers more than 15 million patients. Of 36 eligibility criteria, 11 were not computable and 7 only partially computable, because the data element was absent or the criterion required a subjective judgment by patient or investigator. Effective target populations were 90 patients for the 23 mg arm and 2048 for the 10 mg arm, of whom 38 and 782 met the reconstructed criteria. Race composition diverged sharply from the trial: Hispanics 10.5 to 24.6 percent against 5.5 to 7 percent, Black patients 10.5 to 20.1 percent against 1.9 to 2.3 percent, Asian or Pacific Islander 0 to 1.4 percent against 16.7 to 18.5 percent. A one-arm simulation with proportional sampling on race reproduced the trial control serious adverse event rate closely, 8.9 percent against 8.3 percent with a z test p value of 0.75, across 1000 bootstrap samples. The two-arm simulation used propensity score matching, capped the 23 mg arm at 30 patients and achieved 65 percent post hoc power; serious adverse event rates exceeded the trial's in both arms. Simulated dropout at trial-reported rates lowered mean serious adverse events per patient from 0.64 to 0.19 and 0.23. Efficacy endpoints could not be assessed because Mini-Mental State Examination and Severe Impairment Battery scores are not in structured records.

future_research.gap: No procedure ranks eligibility criteria by how much dropping them distorts the endpoint
future_research.quote: One strategy for future simulation studies is to classify each of the eligibility criteria based on their clinical importance to the simulation study and the endpoints

future_research.gap: Treatment delay and adherence were not modeled because the intervention arm was too small
future_research.quote: Future studies with sufficient sample sizes could conduct more sophisticated analysis based on treatment delay and adherence.

problems.evidence: The resolution rule is stated outright: where a criterion cannot be computed, every candidate is treated as having met it, with willingness and ability to fulfill study requirements given as the worked example. Eleven of 36 criteria enter the reconstructed cohort this way, so patients who would have failed screening are indistinguishable from patients who passed. The consequence is measured rather than hypothesized, since serious adverse event rates rise above the trial's and the incomputable criteria are named as a candidate explanation.
problems.quote: When a criterion is not computable, we consider all candidate patients met that criterion
problems.locator: Results, Computability of eligibility criteria in the original trial

problems.evidence: Two of the incomputable criteria depend on components that no database can hold: a cranial image judged free of focal disease accounting for dementia, and laboratory values judged not clinically significant by the investigator. Substituting universal eligibility does not produce a noisier version of the trial population; it produces a different population defined by what the network happens to record, and only 25 of 36 criteria survive as stated. The resulting arms are then compared against trial results as if they answered the same question.
problems.quote: we found it is difficult to replicate all the eligibility criteria of the original trial. Out of the 36 eligibility criteria, only 25 of them were computable or partially computable against the OneFlorida data.

problems.evidence: A network of more than 15 million patients yields 38 eligible patients in the intervention arm, and the two-arm simulation had to cap that arm at 30 with 65 percent power. The shortage is structural rather than incidental: the 23 mg formulation is reserved in practice for patients stable on 10 mg for three to six months, so the arm the trial randomized into barely exists in routine care. Database size does not translate into a comparison, and no eligible-cohort size threshold was set before the analysis ran.
problems.quote: we only identified 38 patients who took the 23 mg donepezil and met the eligibility criteria of the original trial.

problems.evidence: The outcome is a count of serious adverse events, and the trial's own event labels do not map onto the coding system used for the reconstruction: abnormal behavior and presyncope have no CTCAE counterpart, back pain and fall are recorded as serious in the trial with no grade 4 or 5 CTCAE definition, and the trial's adverse event definitions were unavailable. The comparison of 8.9 percent against 8.3 percent is nevertheless read as agreement, with the phenotype treated as a binary that either fired or did not.
problems.quote: we found that some of the SAEs (e.g., abnormal behavior, presyncope) reported in the trial’s results cannot be mapped to any AE terms in CTCAE, and the definitions of AEs in the original trial were unavailable

problems.evidence: The verdict on the one-arm reconstruction rests on a null hypothesis test between two proportions, 8.9 percent and 8.3 percent, with a p value of 0.75 read as agreement. A failure to reject at n of a few hundred is compatible with a wide range of true differences, and the same reconstruction produced higher mean events per patient than the trial. The two-arm result is graded as not entirely successful, another label rather than a distance between estimands.
problems.quote: the SAE rates in the simulated control were similar to the SAE rates from the original control (8.9% vs. 8.3%), and a z -score test for population proportion had a p -value of 0.75

papers.title: Invited Commentary: The Promise and Pitfalls of Causal Inference With Multivariate Environmental Exposures.
papers.one_line: A commentary on Bayesian g-computation for a hypothetical coal plant decommissioning shows the target trial's intervention arm lies almost entirely outside the observed range of the six metal exposures, so the estimate is produced by model extrapolation rather than by data.
papers.what_was_done: The analysis under review frames six airborne metals linked to three Milwaukee County coal-fired power plants as an environmental mixture and estimates the effect on birth weight of a hypothetical decommissioning before 2010, using Bayesian model averaging over 2 to the 83rd regression specifications built from 83 enumerated quantities, explored with 36,000 random-walk Markov chain Monte Carlo iterations. Because no decommissioning occurred, the intervention is operationalized as a uniform proportional reduction in all six metals; the control arm is the observed mixture. The commentary establishes that the implied post-intervention metal levels fall almost entirely below the range observed anywhere in the study area, so the intervention arm has no representation in the data and every estimate is an extrapolation whose validity rests on the regression model. Sensitivity analyses are shown to move the answer materially: forcing all six exposure main effects into the model roughly doubles the effect estimate relative to the primary analysis, in which substantial posterior weight sits on models that omit some or all of them. Informative priors shrink 14 main-effect coefficients toward a common mean with variance 1, so that a maternal age coefficient is shrunk toward a chromium coefficient. An alternative target trial bounded by observed exposure percentiles is easier to approximate but no longer corresponds to closing a power plant.

future_research.gap: Whether the method behaves differently when exposure can be characterized without extrapolation is untested
future_research.quote: Nonetheless, it is worth considering how the methods outlined here would fare in settings with fewer data limitations

problems.evidence: Positivity fails outright and the failure is visible only because a web figure happens to plot implied against observed exposure levels: the six metal levels under the hypothetical reduction sit almost entirely below anything observed in the study area. What the reported analysis carries instead is a posterior interval and a set of sensitivity analyses, none of which names the census tracts or exposure profiles for which no support exists. The diagnostic that would have identified the problem is not part of the reporting apparatus.
problems.quote: the hypothetical trial entails an “intervention arm” for which there is no representation in the observed data; estimates will necessarily extrapolate to these levels of exposure, and validity is almost entirely dependent upon the adequacy of the statistical model used to perform that extrapolation.
problems.locator: Framing causal questions with mixtures, Defining versus designing the hypothetical trial

problems.evidence: Model averaging over 2 to the 83rd specifications and strong informative priors are the machinery deployed against a problem that is not an estimation problem: the intervention arm is unsupported by data. The verdict is that the flexibility buys nothing against that failure and cannot repair a badly designed hypothetical trial. The simulation offered in support is shown to be uninformative because it evaluates data-generating models that sit inside or near the analysis model class, which is precisely the case where flexible estimation is not being asked to do the work.
problems.quote: these methods are not capable of resolving the friction at the heart of the analysis, and they cannot overcome poor “design” of the hypothetical target trial.
problems.locator: Bayesian causal inference: model averaging and regularization

problems.evidence: The intervention is closing three coal-fired power plants, an assignment made at a facility whose exposure consequences reach census tracts, and its treatment version is supplied by assumption: a uniform proportional reduction in each of the six metals. Whether that is what decommissioning would actually do was left unassessed. Other equally admissible versions, shifting one metal while holding the others fixed, or changing the mixture proportions, define different target trials with different answers, and nothing in the framework selects among them.
problems.quote: Whether this uniform proportional decrease actually corresponds to what would happen upon decommissioning of coal plants is considered in Keil et al.’s paper (3), but detailed assessment of this correspondence was apparently beyond the scope of the investigation.

problems.evidence: The trade is stated in its sharpest form: the version of the target trial that answers the policy question is unsupported by data, and the version bounded by observed exposure percentiles is estimable but no longer about closing power plants. Both estimates can be reported, and nothing separates the loss from abandoning the scientific target from the loss in estimation. A reader given the percentile-bounded secondary analysis has no way to price how far it sits from the decommissioning question.
problems.quote: The readily interpretable framing relative to power plant closures is undercut by the realities of the observed data
problems.locator: Framing causal questions with mixtures, Defining versus designing the hypothetical trial

problems.evidence: One sensitivity analysis doubles the effect estimate: forcing the six exposure main effects into the model returns roughly twice the magnitude of the primary analysis, which had assigned substantial posterior weight to models omitting some or all of them. A second, forcing confounder main effects in, moves it again. There is no principle here that makes the model-averaged specification the default rather than the forced-inclusion one, and the reported sensitivity spread leaves no basis for calling any of the disparate results primary.
problems.quote: As sensitivity analysis H shows, forcing the inclusion of all exposure main effects yields an effect estimate roughly twice the magnitude of that in the primary analysis!
problems.locator: Bayesian causal inference, Bayesian model averaging

papers.title: Mediation effects that emulate a target randomised trial: Simulation-based evaluation of ill-defined interventions on multiple mediators.
papers.one_line: Interventional mediation effects are redefined as contrasts that map to an explicit target trial of hypothetical mediator interventions, so that an ill-defined target such as improving mental health is replaced by a user-specified distributional shift; in the applied example a joint shift of all mediators removes only 23 percent of a 7.2 percent total effect.
papers.what_was_done: Three policy questions are posed and each is mapped to a target trial whose arms are hypothetical interventions shifting one mediator, all mediators jointly, or mediators in sequence, to a user-specified distribution, with the distribution in the unexposed given covariates used as the benchmark. Three estimand assumptions carry the definition: the shift is delivered conditional on baseline covariates only, the achievable target is the unexposed distribution, and under the single-policy premise the intervened mediator is rendered independent of the others. Identification requires assumptions analogous to those of VanderWeele and Hernan, and estimation uses Monte Carlo g-computation with logistic models carrying all two-way interactions; code is released. The application uses 1786 of 1943 Victorian Adolescent Health Cohort Study participants with adolescent self-harm recorded, with 40 imputations for the remaining variables. The total causal effect of adolescent self-harm on mid-life financial hardship is 7.2 percent (95 percent CI minus 1.7 to 16.1). The best single target, university completion, gives 0.9 percent (minus 1.3 to 3.2), a 13 percent reduction; the joint shift gives 1.6 percent (minus 1.6 to 4.9), 23 percent, leaving a direct effect of 5.6 percent (minus 3.1 to 14.3); the sequential policy gives 1.9 percent (minus 1.4 to 5.2), 27 percent. Every interval crosses zero. Mediator correlations under the hypothetical interventions are not identifiable from data.

future_research.gap: The covariate set defining the shift need not equal the confounding adjustment set, and choosing it is unresolved
future_research.quote: further work could consider estimand assumptions that individualise mediator shifts by conditioning on a set of baseline covariates that may overlap with but is not necessarily equal to the minimal confounding adjustment set

future_research.gap: Estimation remains vulnerable to parametric misspecification
future_research.quote: We implemented g-computation using highly flexible regression models, but parametric misspecification bias is still a possibility.

problems.evidence: The unobservable component here is the mediator intervention itself, and the response is not to treat the estimate as a noisy version of an intended effect but to define the data-defined estimand explicitly: shift the mediator distribution to that of the unexposed given covariates, and state the three assumptions that fix it. The resulting quantities, 0.9 percent for university completion and 1.6 percent for the joint shift, are labeled as evidence about intervention targets rather than about interventions. What remains open is that the estimand still depends on unverifiable choices, the benchmark distribution and the mediator dependence structure after intervention, so the substituted estimand is one of a family and nothing prices the distance from the intended one.
problems.quote: the price to pay for considering the joint distribution in the estimand assumptions, even under approach (b) to Question 1, is the need for unverifiable assumptions about the dependence between the mediators under the hypothetical interventions

problems.evidence: Two concrete versions of the same nominal intervention on mental health, widespread psychotherapy and widespread antidepressants, are shown to imply different joint distributions with substance use, and therefore different values for the same defined effect. That is a treatment-version problem with a measurable consequence rather than a definitional complaint. No procedure is offered that would group the versions into a class within which the estimand is stable; the framework instead requires the analyst to assume a correlation structure.
problems.quote: For example, mental health in a subpopulation offered widespread provision of psychotherapy might be more or less correlated (on average) with substance use than in one offered widespread provision of antidepressants.

problems.evidence: The assumption set here splits into three kinds that report identically: identifiability assumptions such as no unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding, which are in principle checkable against subject knowledge; estimand assumptions about the shift and the post-intervention correlations, which are not identifiable from data at all; and assumptions about the hypothetical intervention that cannot be assessed until a concrete intervention exists. The reported effects of 0.9, 1.6 and 1.9 percent carry no marker distinguishing which of the three underwrites which part of the number.
problems.quote: The identification assumptions that concern hypothetical interventions are not assessable without considering a concrete intervention.

problems.evidence: Only one component of the target trial protocol is actually specified, the treatment strategies, and the remaining components are deferred. The reported reductions of 13, 23 and 27 percent therefore carry an unquantified gap between the policy question about young-adult interventions and the estimand that was computed, and no decomposition separates that gap from the estimation uncertainty that the intervals crossing zero already display.
problems.quote: our goal in this work was to define the contrasts of interest in the context of questions regarding ill-defined mediator interventions, acknowledging that this is only one step of a full “target trial approach,”

problems.evidence: Estimation is by Monte Carlo g-computation with logistic models carrying all two-way interactions, chosen for flexibility, and misspecification bias is conceded to remain; doubly or multiply robust machine learning estimation is named as desirable but not implemented. No alternative estimator was run on the same data, so whether the 1.6 percent joint-shift estimate is a property of the estimand or of the model class is not demonstrated either way.
problems.quote: Development of doubly or multiply robust methods for estimation with machine learning, building on recent work,

papers.title: The Target Trial: A Powerful Device Beyond Well-defined Interventions.
papers.one_line: The target trial framework is argued to be a device for specifying estimands rather than a certificate that an intervention is well defined, with the disparity example showing that allowable and nonallowable covariates first appear in different protocol components and therefore belong to different assumption classes.
papers.what_was_done: Two assumption classes are separated: estimand assumptions, which encode what is wanted, including the target population, the interventions compared and the outcomes, and identifiability assumptions, which encode what is known about the data. Mapped to the three-step causal roadmap, estimand assumptions belong to definition and identifiability assumptions to identification, and the observation is that directed acyclic graphs and g-methods have absorbed attention at the second and third steps while the first has been neglected. A target trial protocol is written out for a hypothetical study of intensification of antihypertensive treatment as a mediator of disparities in hypertension control between Black and white patients, with an intervention arm defined by an ill-defined intervention emulated through hypothetical distributional shifts, a comparator arm of Black patients and a second comparator arm of white patients, and causal contrasts named as disparity reduction and residual disparity. Filling in the protocol makes visible that target-allowable covariates first appear under treatment strategies while nonallowable covariates first appear under emulation, so the two sets are doing different jobs. The proposed handling of ill-defined interventions is to posit hypothetical shifts in the intervention target and make estimand assumptions about those shifts, positioned between data-driven causal inference and agent-based modeling. No data are analyzed.

future_research.gap: Ill-defined interventions remain a source of uncertainty that specification does not remove
future_research.quote: The ill-defined nature of the intervention is nonetheless problematic

problems.evidence: The intervention in the worked example, changing physicians' decisions to intensify antihypertensive treatment, has no defined versions; training to raise awareness of unconscious bias is offered as one possibility among many. The position taken is that this should not block the rest of the protocol, so eligibility, target population and contrasts are specified around an intervention whose versions and delivery remain open. That is precisely the configuration the entry names, here for a health-system intervention rather than a drug, and the residual uncertainty is acknowledged rather than resolved.
problems.quote: having an ill-defined intervention should not preclude consideration of all the other aspects of the target-trial specification

problems.evidence: A real separation is supplied: covariates that define the estimand are shown to enter the protocol at a different component from covariates that make it identifiable, so scientific-target choices can be told apart from emulation choices by where they first appear in the table. Applied to existing mediation estimators, this shows that none of them uses covariates appropriately for the question, because they target different estimands. What it does not supply is a size for any component; the decomposition is qualitative and cannot say how much of a reported estimate is target mismatch and how much is estimation.
problems.quote: allowable and nonallowable covariates are of a critically different nature, with allowable covariates pertaining to the target-trial specification, that is, estimand assumptions, while nonallowable covariates pertain to the emulation and required identification assumptions.
problems.locator: Specification of the target trial and its emulation

problems.evidence: Off-the-shelf mediation estimators are shown to emulate target trials implicitly, of interventions unlikely to be relevant to the question asked. An analysis can therefore carry the target-trial property in a technical sense while its estimand answers something else, which is the failure mode the entry names: the association with the framework is not information about what was assumed. The remedy proposed is explicit estimand specification, not a way of reading assumption burden off the label.
problems.quote: only implicitly emulate target trials, and if so of interventions that are unlikely to be relevant.
problems.locator: Recognizing causal inference questions in practice

problems.evidence: The framework's own accounting of what it delivers is that it refines estimands and limits emulation bias while never fixing all the limitations that remain for drawing causal conclusions. Those remaining limitations are not enumerated anywhere in the protocol table, so a completed target trial specification reports the components that were specified and is silent on which assumptions behind them are checkable, which are assumed and which cannot be assessed without a concrete intervention.
problems.quote: keeping in mind that this will never fix all the limitations that must still be considered for the purpose of drawing causal conclusions.

papers.title: Statins as Potential Chemoprevention or Therapeutic Agents in Cancer: a Model for Evaluating Repurposed Drugs.
papers.one_line: Evidence for repurposing statins in cancer is assembled across preclinical work, trial meta-analyses, Mendelian randomization and target trial emulation, and the two emulations that exist, one of 733,804 UK adults and one of 17,372 SEER patients with an overall survival hazard ratio of 1.00, both contradict the earlier observational literature.
papers.what_was_done: A decision model for repurposed drugs is proposed and then applied to statins in cancer prevention and treatment, on the stated premise that the conventional development pathway does not fit repurposing and no consensus exists on what evidence should precede a phase III trial. Four evidence streams are weighed. Cardiovascular trial meta-analyses contribute cancer incidence after randomization, with 1.4 percent developing cancer per year in the Cholesterol Treatment Trialists data and no information on statin continuation after diagnosis. A target trial emulation in 733,804 UK adults found little evidence that statins affect cancer incidence over 10 years, and attributed prior positive observational findings to deviation from trial design principles; its eligibility criterion of LDL cholesterol below 5 mmol per liter is flagged as channeling patients with diabetes into the statin arm. In the adjuvant setting a single emulation exists, 17,372 SEER patients across colorectal, breast, prostate and bladder cancer stages I to III, in which statin initiation within six months of diagnosis did not improve three-year survival, overall survival hazard ratio 1.00 (0.88 to 1.15). Mendelian randomization on HMGCR variants gives 0.99 (0.95 to 1.02) for overall cancer in 6528 cases, 0.97 (0.94 to 1.00) for prostate cancer in 22,773 cases, 0.86 (0.73 to 1.02) for breast cancer in 122,977 cases, and 0.60 (0.43 to 0.83) for epithelial ovarian cancer. Most of the observational literature compares current including prevalent users against never users.

future_research.gap: Only one tumor-site set has been examined under an emulated protocol
future_research.quote: The application of this methodology to other cancer types would be welcome in informing the decision to proceed to a trial.
future_research.locator: Pharmaco-epidemiological research in the adjuvant setting of cancer

problems.evidence: The stated reason a model is needed at all is that no agreed standard exists for what evidence must be in hand before committing to a phase III trial of a repurposed drug. Nothing in what follows supplies one: the closing recommendation is to weigh evidence from all sources as systematically and fairly as possible, tumor site by tumor site. An emulation returning an overall survival hazard ratio of 1.00 with bounds 0.88 to 1.15 across 17,372 patients therefore has no threshold against which it counts as a stop or a go.
problems.quote: there is currently no consensus on establishing the evidence base before embarking on a large, resource intensive, potential practice changing phase III randomised controlled trial

problems.evidence: Exactly one emulation exists in the adjuvant setting, covering four tumor sites at stages I to III with three-year follow-up, and its null result is being used to inform whether trials in other sites are warranted. The extension is asserted as desirable rather than argued: nothing states what property of colorectal, breast, prostate and bladder cancer makes the emulation's success transfer, and the accompanying caveat that longer follow-up matters applies to the source result too.
problems.quote: The application of this methodology to other cancer types would be welcome in informing the decision to proceed to a trial.
problems.locator: Pharmaco-epidemiological research in the adjuvant setting of cancer

problems.evidence: The dominant observational design compares current and prevalent statin users against never users, which is identified as answering a different question from the trial one about allocation at a fixed start. That is scientific-target mismatch, and it is named as a source of the discrepancy with randomized evidence that is distinct from residual confounding. No decomposition puts a size on either component, so a reader cannot tell how much of the gap between the earlier positive observational literature and the null emulation came from the question and how much from adjustment.
problems.quote: This answers a fundamentally different question to that posed by RCTs: whether allocation to statins (new users) compared with no statins at the point of randomization affects survival.
problems.locator: Pharmaco-epidemiological research in the adjuvant setting of cancer

problems.evidence: The 733,804-adult emulation restricted eligibility on a recorded LDL cholesterol value below 5 mmol per liter. Both the requirement that a value exist and the threshold itself select on healthcare contact and on indication: statins are given to patients with diabetes irrespective of LDL, so the criterion channels a group with elevated cancer risk into the treated arm. The distortion is identified after the fact in a narrative reading of another team's protocol, with no diagnostic that would have surfaced it during design.
problems.quote: Eligibility criteria included LDL cholesterol level < 5 mmol L −1 ,which may have introduced some confounding, channelling people with diabetes into the statin group

problems.evidence: Mendelian randomization is the proxy design available for this question and it returns numbers that could calibrate the emulation, 0.99 for overall cancer and 0.86 for breast cancer against the null adjuvant hazard ratio of 1.00. The two streams are instead weighed side by side in prose, with the choice among them left to a systematic and fair reading. No workflow integrates the genetic evidence into the emulation as a bound on unmeasured confounding, and validation data for the statin-cancer question is not part of the emulation protocol at all.
problems.quote: The challenge is, therefore, to weigh up the evidence from all sources as systematically and fairly as possible

papers.title: Emulating Target Trials to Improve Causal Inference From Agent-Based Models.
papers.one_line: Agent-based models are designed to emulate cluster-randomized, network-randomized, two-stage and ring-vaccination target trials so that simulated results carry the four partial-interference estimands, direct, disseminated, total and overall, rather than an unlabeled association.
papers.what_was_done: The proposal is that an agent-based model should be written against a target trial protocol, with inclusion and exclusion criteria, treatment and comparator strategies expressed as simulation algorithms, outcomes with competing-event handling, follow-up start and end, and a named estimand. The estimands imported are the partial-interference set of Halloran and Struchiner: a direct effect of receiving versus not receiving intervention at a fixed cluster coverage, a disseminated effect of cluster coverage on an unintervened member, a total effect combining both, and an overall effect comparing all-control to all-intervention clusters. The claimed advantage over emulation with observational data is that a simulation can be built to match a two-stage or cluster-randomized design exactly, so identification of the four effects follows without further confounding argument. The worked case is a published sexual-network model of preexposure prophylaxis among men who have sex with men, in which increasing component coverage lowers HIV incidence among unrandomized members while reducing the marginal benefit of PrEP to any individual. The stated cost is parameterization: transmission inputs may not be estimable from any dataset, and interference patterns can differ so fundamentally between populations that the potential outcomes themselves stop transferring. No estimate, interval or calibration check appears.

future_research.gap: Transportability methods exist for individually randomized trials but not for the cluster and network designs the framework relies on
future_research.quote: Methods are being developed to address the challenges of transportability and generalizability in individual-level randomized trials
future_research.locator: Interference and the potential outcomes framework

future_research.gap: The inputs the causal estimands depend on may not be estimable from any dataset
future_research.quote: The main challenge for emulating randomized trials with ABMs will be obtaining empirical data to parameterize the model inputs
future_research.locator: Emulating target trials with agent-based models

problems.evidence: This is a concrete route out of the no-interference assumption rather than a restatement of it: four estimands under partial interference are named, and each is tied to a randomized design that identifies it, with two-stage randomization identifying the direct, disseminated and total effects with no further confounding argument. What it does not close is the structural precondition. The estimands require a partition into clusters with no cross-cluster connection, and specifying the interference pattern requires the types, frequencies and reasons for contacts or the full contact network, which the same text concedes may not be estimable. Nothing addresses the entry's second clause, that cloning individuals into per-protocol arms can produce joint strategies nobody could implement.
problems.quote: To parameterize interference, a model would need to include specification of the types, frequencies, and reasons for contacts between individuals
problems.locator: Interference and the potential outcomes framework

problems.evidence: Under interference the transport problem is worse than a reweighting of effect modifiers: the potential outcomes are indexed by other people's exposures, so a population whose contact structure differs can fail to admit the same potential outcomes at all. The available machinery is conceded to cover individually randomized trials only, leaving the cluster and network designs on which the four estimands depend with no transport method. The accounting the entry asks for is therefore not merely absent but has no defined form here.
problems.quote: In some cases, the patterns of interference may differ in fundamental ways between populations, such that the definition of the potential outcomes (which depends on the interference pattern) no longer applies to the new population.
problems.locator: Interference and the potential outcomes framework

problems.evidence: The intervention here is a coverage level within a sexual network component, not a treatment given to a person, and the assignment unit is the component. The framework relies on specifying a clear causal contrast, but records an unresolved disagreement about whether a well-defined intervention must be humanly feasible, with three reasons given for rejecting both sides of that dispute rather than a rule for deciding it. For a coverage-level intervention there is no statement of what its versions are or how a component boundary is drawn in a real population.
problems.quote: Some researchers have stated that a requisite for a well-defined intervention is that it be humanly feasible.
problems.locator: The target trial framework for causal inference

problems.evidence: The model is used to produce named causal estimands while some of its inputs are conceded to be unobtainable from any data and to be filled from experts' best estimates. No fidelity criterion is proposed that a simulation must clear before its output is read as a direct or disseminated effect, and the framework's stated contribution is clarifying which parameters are needed and what bias guessed parameters may cause, not bounding that bias.
problems.quote: indeed many inputs can never be obtained empirically
problems.locator: Emulating target trials with agent-based models

papers.title: A Narrative Review of Methods for Causal Inference and Associated Educational Resources.
papers.one_line: A narrative review aimed at root cause analysis with secondary data surveys causal inference methods and training materials, and reports that specifying a target trial is among the most fundamental steps yet receives little or no coverage in the existing literature.
papers.what_was_done: The review is written for clinical researchers with basic statistics or epidemiology training and for statisticians working with them, on the premise that observational root cause analysis of adverse events requires methods outside the standard toolbox. The target trial is presented as the first move, converting a poorly defined question such as whether shorter physician shifts are better into an estimable one about assigning physicians to longer shifts, with participants who always receive the intervention excluded by design. The seven-step causal roadmap of Peterson and van der Laan is set out, from causal model through identifiability to estimation and interpretation. Propensity score methods are covered along with doubly robust and covariate balancing variants, causal graphs and structural equations, instrumental variables illustrated by Vietnam draft status, and g-methods, marginal structural models and targeted maximum likelihood for time-varying exposures. Five questions are offered for choosing among them, covering exposure timing, estimand consistency, assumption plausibility, parametric versus nonparametric modeling and whether conditioning achieves conditional independence, with the explicit statement that answering them does not identify which method works best. Educational resources are catalogued, including four Coursera courses attended by nearly 40,000 students and more than 3000 causal inference tutorials published in four years. No data are analyzed.

future_research.gap: Target trial specification is absent from the teaching literature it surveys
future_research.quote: even the most fundamental aspects of causal inference (eg, framing the causal question as a target trial) often receive little or no coverage.

problems.evidence: Five questions are supplied for choosing an estimator and then explicitly disclaimed as unable to identify which method works best; they narrow the field rather than select from it. Propensity methods, doubly robust and covariate balancing variants, instrumental variables, g-methods, marginal structural models and targeted maximum likelihood are all presented as admissible, each carrying a different estimand, with no default and no requirement that a study demonstrate its choice was immaterial.
problems.quote: The questions about assumptions for a given statistical model are difficult to answer and often not directly testable.
problems.locator: Other statistical models for causal inference

problems.evidence: Studies of the same clinical question are shown to be incomparable when the estimands differ, and the closing advice is that apparent differences between studies may be an artifact of that mismatch. Nothing separates the components of the difference: an estimand chosen because it was estimable, a target trial whose eligibility restrictions moved the population, and estimation error all present as a single divergence between two published numbers.
problems.quote: otherwise, apparent differences may be the result of comparing apples with oranges.

problems.evidence: Data fitness enters as one consideration among several when selecting a statistical model, and the remedy offered when assumptions are not supported is to impose restrictions in the target trial design rather than to stop. That converts a data deficiency into a redefinition of the question, and no threshold is named at which secondary data are unfit for a root cause analysis of an adverse event.
problems.quote: Selection of the appropriate statistical model must also consider which assumptions can be reasonably supported by the available data, either directly or after introducing restrictions as part of the target trial design.

problems.evidence: Every method surveyed carries assumptions the review describes as difficult to answer and often not directly testable, and the instrumental variables entry adds instrument strength and conditional independence from the outcome to the list. The reporting apparatus offered is the seven-step roadmap, whose final step is interpretation in light of the assumptions, with no structure that marks which of them a given analysis was able to diagnose.
problems.quote: The causal effect therefore needs to be specified, implemented, and interpreted in a consistent manner with the research question; this issue is often ignored in the literature when applying causal inference methods.
problems.locator: Defining causal effects using a target trial and causal road map, The target trial

papers.title: Conceptualising natural and quasi experiments in public health.
papers.one_line: Natural experiment studies in public health are recast as a study design rather than a toolbox of estimators and mapped onto the seven target trial protocol components, with the as-if randomization assumption conceded to be unprovable and placed on a continuum of plausibility.
papers.what_was_done: A search of Medline, Embase and Google Scholar supplemented by grey literature was used to reconcile competing definitions of natural experiment studies and align them to the target trial framework. Three conceptualizations are separated: the analytic one that identifies natural experiments with difference-in-differences, interrupted time series, regression discontinuity, synthetic controls and instrumental variables; the Dunning one that requires a defensible argument for as-if randomization; and the MRC one that requires only that the event lie outside researcher control. The resulting position is that what separates such studies from randomized trials is loss of control over allocation, and what separates them from other observational designs is that they evaluate a defined event or process producing exposure differences. A table maps the seven target trial components, eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, assignment procedures, follow-up period, outcome, causal contrasts and analysis plan, onto natural experiment studies, with sensitivity analysis recommendations derived from Rosenbaum attached to each. A worked alignment of a UK national minimum wage evaluation is supplied in a supplement, comparing wage recipients up to 110 percent of pre-intervention wage against people just above the threshold and against eligible people in noncompliant firms. No effect estimate is produced and no threshold is set at which a study fails the framework.

future_research.gap: Evidence grading systems do not distinguish natural experiment studies from other observational designs
future_research.quote: the specific inclusion of NES in this system might improve the rating of the evidence from these study designs.

future_research.gap: The core identifying assumption of the design cannot be verified
future_research.quote: Because the concept of ‘as-if’ randomization is difficult, if not impossible to prove, it should be thought of along a ‘continuum of plausibility’
future_research.locator: Results, Part 2. A target trial framework for natural experiment studies

problems.evidence: A protocol template is supplied for exactly the class of interventions the entry names: policy and health system reforms that cannot be manipulated experimentally. Each of the seven target trial components is given a question set and sensitivity analysis recommendations, and a national minimum wage evaluation is aligned to it. What it does not close is the definition of treatment versions and assignment units. The assignment procedure component is discharged by an argument for as-if randomization rather than by naming who or what is the unit assigned, and a wage increase up to 110 percent of baseline is treated as one strategy without specifying the versions it comprises.
problems.quote: Natural or quasi experiments are appealing for public health research because they enable the evaluation of events or interventions that are difficult or impossible to manipulate experimentally, such as many policy and health system reforms.

problems.evidence: The framework's own summary of its recommendations is that none of them individually removes bias and that a study need not implement all of them to support a causal claim. That leaves no way to read off which assumptions in a given natural experiment were checked, which were assumed, and which are undiagnosable in principle; the as-if randomization assumption, conceded to be unprovable, is reported in the same table as sensitivity analyses that do return a number.
problems.quote: None of the recommendations outlined in Table 1 will by themselves eliminate bias in a NES, but neither is it required to implement all of them to be able to make a causal claim with some confidence.

problems.evidence: The stated motivation for tightening the definition is that the natural experiment label is already being applied to studies of exposure variation with no event at all, and that the label itself confers an unearned appearance of experimental status. That is the failure mode the entry names, observed in a neighboring design vocabulary: a name is doing the work that an assumption audit should do, and the proposed remedy is a stricter definition rather than a measurement of assumption burden.
problems.quote: A more stringent classification of NES as a type of study design, rather than a collection of analytic tools, is important because it prevents attempts to incorrectly cover observational studies with a ‘glow of experimental legitimacy’
problems.locator: Results, Part 1. Conceptualisations of natural experiments

problems.evidence: The proposal for how evidence users should treat these studies is an ordering, with well conducted randomized trials first, natural experiments second and other observational studies third, offered as an extension to GRADE that does not yet exist. No threshold is given at which residual confounding is small enough or the sensitivity analyses sufficient; the recommendation is that inclusion in the grading system might improve the rating, not that a stated bar must be cleared.
problems.quote: the specific inclusion of NES in this system might improve the rating of the evidence from these study designs.

problems.evidence: The recommended practice is a set of sensitivity analyses each aimed at one potential bias, combined additively to strengthen a claim. Nothing addresses the case where unmeasured confounding, selection into the exposed group and outcome misclassification are all present at once, and the framework concedes that because each analysis depends on an assumed maximum size for its own omitted bias, none of them rules out residual bias.
problems.quote: Each sensitivity analysis aims to minimise ambiguity of a particular potential bias or biases, and as such a combination of selected sensitivity analyses can strengthen causal claims

papers.title: Contextualizing single-arm trials with real-world data: An emulated target trial comparing therapies for neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
papers.one_line: A single trial arm of 65 bevacizumab-treated eyes was compared against EHR-derived aflibercept controls under four different randomization-emulation methods, and the four methods disagreed: propensity score matching alone failed to establish noninferiority and was the only method that created a baseline imbalance where none existed before.
papers.what_was_done: The bevacizumab arm of the ABC randomized trial (n = 65, treated 2006 to 2008) was contrasted with aflibercept-treated eyes drawn from Medisoft ophthalmology EHRs across 27 English sites (2012 to 2018) for week 54 visual acuity. Of 31,151 aflibercept-initiating eyes, 26,680 (86 percent) were excluded, 20,823 for ABC criteria and 5,857 for emulated-trial criteria, leaving 4,471 (14 percent); a further 186 were trimmed for nonoverlapping propensity scores. Four methods for emulating randomization on age, sex and baseline ETDRS letters were run in parallel: unconditional analysis (65 versus 4,471), inverse probability of treatment weighting (pseudo-population 131 versus 8,506), exact matching (43 versus 43) and propensity score matching (65 versus 65), with the propensity model trained on all 131 ABC subjects. Noninferiority was declared against a margin of minus four ETDRS letters. Three methods supported noninferiority; propensity score matching did not, returning a mean difference of minus 0.1 letters with wide bounds, and it left age imbalanced while introducing an imbalance in baseline acuity that had been balanced beforehand. Protocol alignment moved mean baseline acuity from 56 ETDRS letters among real-world initiators to 51 to 53 in the external arms. Eligibility criteria absent from the EHR were handled by assumption. No per-protocol effect was estimated and no reference two-arm trial existed for triangulation.

future_research.gap: No reference trial exists against which the emulated comparison can be calibrated
future_research.quote: With no existing trials comparing the efficacy of bevacizumab to aflibercept and with bevacizumab not being prescribed per ABC protocol during routine health care, it was not possible for us to triangulate our findings against a reference standard.
future_research.locator: Discussion, Unanswered questions and future research

problems.evidence: Four estimators targeting the same estimand on the same data return different conclusions: unconditional, IPTW and exact matching all support noninferiority against the minus four letter margin, while propensity score matching does not. The divergence is not attributed to a defect that could have been detected in advance; matching is the only method that induced an imbalance in baseline acuity that was absent before adjustment, which is discovered after the fact. No prespecified rule selects among the four, and the reported conclusion rests on three of them agreeing.
problems.quote: Notably, of all methods for emulating randomization, PSM was the only to lead to inexchangeability in baseline read, and more curiously was that this was being exchangeable prior to emulating randomization.
problems.locator: Discussion, In context with the evidence base

problems.evidence: Trial criteria that the ophthalmology EHR does not record were resolved by assuming they were met: inadequate contraception in premenopausal women, contraindications, active infection and recent stroke or cardiac event are all inferred to be absent from the fact that treatment was given. Nothing in the data distinguishes an eye whose treating clinician checked and cleared these from an eye where the check was never recorded, and the 4,471-eye eligible pool is defined by that inference.
problems.quote: are implied through treatment not to be present (inadequate contraception in premenopausal women, no contraindications or active infection, or recent stroke or cardiac event)

problems.evidence: A pool of 31,151 treated eyes yields 4,471 eligible, and the analysis that actually drives the comparison shrinks further: exact matching leaves 43 versus 43 and propensity score matching 65 versus 65, because the trial arm caps the achievable sample at 65 regardless of database size. The confidence bounds for both matching analyses are visibly wider than for the unconditional and weighted analyses, and the paper attributes this directly to the sample reduction.
problems.quote: Another notable limitation of matching in general is the reduced sample size leading to widened confidence bounds and potential biases from discarding unmatched observations.
problems.locator: Discussion, In context with the evidence base

problems.evidence: The trial arm is drawn from 2006 to 2008 and the external arm from 2012 to 2018, and protocol alignment shifts mean baseline acuity from 56 ETDRS letters among real-world initiators to 51 to 53 in the aligned external arms, matching the ABC population mean of 51. Both moves are sampling operations layered on top of the confounding adjustment, and the direction of the resulting bias is reasoned about qualitatively, that a contemporaneous sample would shrink toward the null, with no accounting that separates the transport component from the exchangeability component of the reported estimate.
problems.quote: the alignment of the real‐world cohorts to the ABC trial population (mean baseline read 51) lowers the mean from 56 ETDRS in those initiating treatment in the real‐world to 51–53 for the external cohorts.

problems.evidence: Positivity is reported as a one-line pass covering all levels of the three confounders, yet 186 of 4,471 eyes were removed beforehand precisely because their propensity scores had no counterpart in the trial arm. The diagnostic names neither which age, sex and baseline acuity combinations were discarded nor what the remaining estimate therefore applies to; the trimming is described as a preprocessing step rather than as a restriction of the target population.
problems.quote: The synthetic distribution tails not overlapping with the propensity scores of the bevacizumab arm were trimmed prior to weighting and matching.
problems.locator: Methods, Inverse propensity score weighting and propensity score matching

problems.evidence: The evidentiary warrant offered for the methods used here is a tally: prior work emulating single-arm trials with external controls agreed in 10 of 11 cases. A count of agreements carries no information about how far the disagreeing estimate sat from its trial, nor about whether the emulated and trial estimands were the same quantity, and it is used to license a new comparison in a different disease area for which no trial reference exists at all.
problems.quote: The paper reports, through alignment of protocols and propensity‐based adjustment, concordance in 10 out of the 11 trials emulated.
problems.locator: Discussion, In context with the evidence base
